security_audit.summary: The many Ruby backtick findings are mostly markdown formatting false positives, but the skill still contains real operational risk. Confirmed issues include privileged Docker setup, sudo-based tool installation, remote installer execution, persistent dotfile changes, temporary analysis artifacts, and a workflow for executing untrusted binaries. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Privileged Docker setup is included in the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Move binfmt registration to manual documentation, require explicit user confirmation, and prefer unprivileged containers for routine analysis.

remediation.issue: Remote installer output is executed directly by bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash setup with pinned release downloads, checksums, manual review steps, and non-executing install instructions.

remediation.issue: Tool setup uses sudo and writes persistent shell, GDB, and radare2 configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Gate every privileged or dotfile-changing command, show exact diffs, create backups, and avoid automatic execution by agents.
Default to no network, read-only mounts, private work directories, resource limits, command previews, and explicit approval before each execution.

remediation.issue: Memory dumps and traces may be written to shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Write analysis artifacts to a private project directory with restricted permissions and an explicit retention policy.

content.value_statement: Unknown binaries are hard to explain without a repeatable workflow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through triage, static analysis, dynamic testing, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Identifies binary architecture, ABI, dependencies, imports, exports, and strings.
Guides radare2 and Ghidra workflows for function mapping and decompilation.
Plans controlled dynamic analysis with QEMU, GDB, Frida, strace, Docker, and nsjail.
Correlates static and runtime observations into hypotheses with confidence levels.
Generates structured reverse engineering reports with evidence chains.
Provides setup guidance for common reverse engineering tools and cross-architecture sysroots.
limitations: Dynamic execution requires explicit human approval and a hardened sandbox.
Tool setup may require privileged system changes outside the skill environment.
Analysis quality depends on available tools, symbols, architecture support, and sample behavior.
The skill does not prove malware intent without supporting evidence from analysis.

use_cases.title: Triage Unknown Firmware Tools
use_cases.description: Identify architecture, libc, dependencies, and likely capabilities before deeper reverse engineering.

use_cases.title: Map Suspicious Binary Behavior
use_cases.description: Combine strings, imports, cross-references, and controlled runtime traces to explain what a binary does.

use_cases.title: Prepare Evidence-Based Reports
use_cases.description: Turn reverse engineering notes into a structured report with findings, confidence, and remaining questions.

prompt_templates.title: Start Basic Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with an unknown executable and no prior notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this binary at a triage level. Identify file type, architecture, ABI, dependencies, strings of interest, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Perform Static Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Triage is complete and deeper code understanding is needed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use static analysis to map key functions, imports, strings, cross-references, and likely data flow. Do not execute the binary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Dynamic Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Runtime behavior must be verified with approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sandboxed dynamic analysis plan for this binary. Include risks, isolation settings, commands to preview, and evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Triage, static analysis, and dynamic observations are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a final binary analysis report with confirmed facts, hypotheses, confidence levels, behavioral summary, security findings, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Analyze an ARM firmware utility with unknown behavior.
output: The report identifies the binary as ARM 32-bit little-endian with musl libc.
It lists imported networking functions, file paths, and candidate configuration strings.
It recommends static analysis first and dynamic testing only after sandbox approval.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a binary contacts the network.
output: The analysis links socket and connect imports to a specific function.
Runtime observations confirm one outbound connection attempt in the sandbox.
The conclusion includes confidence, evidence sources, and remaining unknowns.

output_examples.input: Prepare a stakeholder report from reverse engineering notes.
output: The output summarizes purpose, capabilities, file access, network behavior, and security concerns.
Each conclusion includes traceable evidence and a calibrated confidence level.
Open questions and recommended follow-up work are separated from confirmed findings.

best_practices: Start with read-only triage and static analysis before any execution.
Use explicit human approval, network isolation, read-only mounts, and timeouts for dynamic tests.
Record facts, hypotheses, confidence, and evidence sources after each phase.
anti_patterns: Do not run unknown binaries natively before reviewing sandbox controls.
Do not treat strings, imports, or decompiler output as confirmed behavior without corroboration.
Do not install privileged tools or remote scripts automatically from the skill workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill execute binaries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requires explicit human approval before execution and recommends sandbox controls.

faq.question: Can it analyze malware samples?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in an isolated analysis environment with network and filesystem controls.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references radare2, rabin2, Ghidra, QEMU, GDB, Frida, strace, Docker, nsjail, jq, and binutils.

faq.question: Can it work without radare2 or Ghidra?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides fallback commands using file, readelf, objdump, nm, strings, and ldd.

faq.question: Does it provide final reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a synthesis phase for evidence-based reports with confidence and recommendations.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are executing untrusted binaries, privileged Docker setup, remote installers, sudo commands, and dotfile changes.
